# Signet

> Signet lets a dApp team seal each release of its website on X Layer (file hashes, the contracts and spenders the site may ask a wallet to sign for, the outside origins it may use). A TapeOut circuit decides when a release goes live (CI can only propose and publish; humans approve; risky changes wait 24 h). Users who run the Guard browser extension have every page and every signature checked against the sealed release; the signing decision comes from a second TapeOut circuit. Users without Guard are NOT protected at signing; a watchtower alerts the team instead.

Status (2026-11-18): the release-policy circuit (#6 on processor #101, 0x73153e5fd2Acac604D49d6ca9fea27b750718F22) is on X Layer mainnet and verified on all 512 inputs. Signet's contracts, the Guard decision circuit, the gateway, the dashboard and the watchtower run on a local fork of X Layer (staging); the mainnet deployment is planned and costed (about 0.0022 OKB) but not sent. Guard has been tested with a mock wallet, not MetaMask.
